sessions.title: 100 Million Bugs Later: A Field Report From the Agentic Era (sponsored by CodeRabbit)
sessions.abstract:
CodeRabbit reviews code generated by major coding agents: 30M+ pull requests and 200K+ independent code reviews each day across open source and enterprises. As agentic development accelerated, PR volume grew 4x while review rounds per PR fell 20%. AI-co-authored PRs carry about 1.7x more issues and up to 2.74x more security issues than human-written code.
David Loker, CodeRabbit VP of Applied AI, shares 12 months of review telemetry behind 100M caught bugs—and the enterprise pattern it reveals: heterogeneous coding-agent stacks are the end state. He introduces Agentic Change Management: an independent, agent-agnostic quality gate that assesses every change, surfaces what needs human attention, and explains what it approves. Leave with a vendor-neutral framework for scaling an agentic SDLC without sacrificing quality, security, or control. This presentation is brought to you by CodeRabbit, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Build and Deploy an eve Agent with Vercel and AWS (sponsored by Vercel)
sessions.abstract: Build and deploy a personalized eve agent with Vercel and AWS in this hands-on innovation lab. You'll start from zero, scaffold an open-source eve.dev agent framework, configure it with your own instructions, connect it to Amazon Bedrock through Vercel Al Gateway, and deploy it to Vercel. The lab is designed for a range of builders: beginners and non-technical users can quickly build and launch a functional agent, while more advanced engineers can explore how the same agent architecture can connect to AWS services and enterprise data sources such as Aurora, S3, or DynamoDB using Vercel and AWS native integration and advanced Vercel networking. Along the way, you'll learn how Vercel and AWS work together to help teams move from Al prototype to production-ready application. Workstations are provided; no reservation needed. Labs are 30-60 min. This presentation is brought to you by Vercel, an AWS Partner.

By the end of this session you will have both practical experience adding Network Firewall to existing environments and reusable patterns ready for your own infrastructure.

sessions.title: GPU cluster failure patterns on AWS: observe, diagnose, recover
sessions.abstract: At scale, GPU clusters fail in ways single-node debugging never taught you: NCCL timeouts that are actually storage problems, DataLoader forks that silently hang collectives, and GPUs that pass every health check yet corrupt your results. In this hands-on builders session, you diagnose these failures on NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances with Elastic Fabric Adapter. Read NCCL debug logs, interpret all-reduce bus bandwidth against per-instance baselines, and run open-source health checks that catch faults before your jobs do. You leave with a failure-signature runbook and a triage method distilled from operating large GPU fleets on AWS.

Learn how AI-powered agents, explainable workflows, and governed human-in-the-loop processes are driving operational efficiency, enhancing regulatory confidence, improving audit readiness, and laying the foundation for autonomous finance operations. sessions.abstract: AI-generated code is scaling fast, but its security performance is not keeping up. Across more than 100 models tested since 2023, the average security pass rate remains stuck at 56%, even as syntax performance approaches perfection. For security leaders, this is no longer a developer tooling discussion. It is a verification, release-control, and accountability issue. In this session, Veracode leaders unpack the findings from the 2026 GenAI Code Security Report and turn them into practical actions for secure software delivery at scale. Whether you’re a developer, security lead, or business decision-maker, this session will help you navigate the real-world security implications of GenAI in your development workflow. This presentation is brought to you by Veracode, Inc., an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Journey to Post Quantum (PQ) Authentication in AWS
sessions.abstract: You use certificates for identity, keys for token signing, and long-lived roots of trust. Now you need to migrate to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) for authentication. In this session, learn how AWS helps you start and stay PQ-ready while preserving backwards compatibility, performance, and AI-friendly security by default. We will demystify the present state and future trajectory of PQ authentication. We discuss the updated CNSA 2.0 dates when RSA and EC will no longer satisfy authentication requirements and the uncertainty around PQ public certificate formats and Merkle Trees in non-browser scenarios.
